title: Tensions rise in July 2008 as Russian jets violate Georgian airspace
body:
Tension in the Georgian conflict zones increased steadily through the summer of 2008. On 26 June Russian President Dmitry Medvedev met Abkhaz leader Sergei Bagapsh in Moscow, the first meeting between a Russian president and an Abkhaz leader. On 3 July a South Ossetian official, Nodar Bibilov, died in an explosion; Ossetian leaders blamed Georgia, blocked roads, and an assassination attempt on the pro-Tbilisi official Dmitry Sanakoyev followed. On 6 July six people were killed in a cafe explosion in Abkhazia's Gali district.

On 8 July 2008 Georgia alleged that four Russian fighter jets had violated its airspace. Russia acknowledged the violation, which Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty described as the first time Moscow had conceded one. On 9 July US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, visiting Tbilisi, urged Russia to help resolve the problem, and Georgia recalled its ambassador from Russia for consultations.

In mid-July joint Georgian-US training took place at Vaziani, while Russian forces concentrated in the North Caucasus for possible peacemaking operations. Between 17 and 19 July German Foreign Minister Frank-Walter Steinmeier proposed a three-stage de-escalation plan for Abkhazia, which neither Sukhumi nor Moscow welcomed. Hostilities in the Georgian-Ossetian conflict zone broke out on 1 August 2008, when Georgian villages were bombed.
